acceptance.given: Package A tests use disposable fixture roots containing intentional corruptions and synthetic credentials as negative inputs.

oracle.expected: Static inspection of the declared test helpers and fixture data confirms that every intentional corruption and synthetic credential is confined to disposable test data.
forbidden: Any intentional corruption or synthetic credential is treated as production data or a real credential.
The boundary is inferred solely from a validator runtime return value without checking test and fixture placement.
oracle.observable: The test helper and fixture sources show corruptions and synthetic credentials only within the declared disposable test-data boundary.

acceptance.then: The boundary assertion passes only when all inspected corruptions and synthetic credentials remain test-only; otherwise it emits a boundary diagnostic and fails.
acceptance.when: During static Package A test validation, inspect the declared capability and migration test modules, support helper, and fixture inputs for containment within disposable test data.

failure_intents.selector_intent: The test-only boundary selector must fail with an observable boundary diagnostic when an intentional corruption or synthetic credential is moved into or classified as production data.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add a static boundary assertion that confines intentional corruptions and synthetic credentials to disposable test data and rejects production-data or real-credential treatment.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persistent state or schema migration is introduced; rollback removes the boundary rule while preserving existing interfaces.

slice_hint.state_transition: Negative inputs remain confined to disposable fixture data before and after validation, with no production-data or credential state introduced.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted capability and migration test selectors complete with a boundary assertion that rejects any corruption or synthetic credential outside disposable test data, and the terminal Package A suite preserves that result.
